target.title: fix(logs): preserve log tails across short reads
target.body:
## What Problem This Solves

Fixes an issue where users reading OpenClaw logs through the CLI, Gateway logs method, or diagnostic support export could receive an incomplete log tail when the filesystem returns a short positional read for the bounded tail window.

## Why This Change Was Made

The shared log-tail reader now fills the requested bounded read window before decoding and splitting lines, matching the existing gateway diagnostic tail-reader invariant. This stays local to log-tail read completeness and does not change cursor, reset, truncation, schema, CLI, or UI behavior.

## User Impact

Log views and support bundles now preserve the recent log lines available within the configured byte budget even when the underlying file read completes in smaller chunks.

## Evidence

- Claim proved: the configured log-tail path preserves complete recent lines through `readConfiguredLogTail`, Gateway `logs.tail`, and diagnostic support export while the underlying log-file reads repeatedly return only four bytes.
- Current-head real behavior proof at `0ca736b6b95204b212a5d0f71d9d782a7452172f`: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` used a temporary `OPENCLAW_STATE_DIR` with `logging.file=<temp-state>/logs/openclaw.log`, wrote a real JSONL log file, patched `fs.promises.open` only for that log file to force four-byte positional reads, then called the current branch's real `readConfiguredLogTail`, Gateway `logsHandlers["logs.tail"]`, and `writeDiagnosticSupportExport`. The proof removed the temporary state after completion and did not commit artifacts.
- Redacted terminal output excerpt showing repeated short reads through the real Gateway consumer path and the complete after-fix tail:

```json
{
  "proofMode": "temporary state dir, real log file, fs.promises.open wrapped to force 4-byte positional reads for the log file only",
  "logFile": "<temp-state>/logs/openclaw.log",
  "maxBytes": 326,
  "shortReadDiagnostics": {
    "gateway logs.tail": {
      "totalReads": 83,
      "shortReads": 81,
      "events": [
        { "position": 109, "requested": 326, "actual": 4, "forcedCap": 4, "short": true },
        { "position": 113, "requested": 322, "actual": 4, "forcedCap": 4, "short": true },
        { "position": 117, "requested": 318, "actual": 4, "forcedCap": 4, "short": true }
      ]
    }
  },
  "gatewayLogsTail": {
    "ok": true,
    "lineCount": 3,
    "messages": [
      "proof-short-read-one",
      "proof-short-read-two",
      "proof-short-read-three"
    ],
    "completeTail": true,
    "truncated": true,
    "reset": false
  },
  "diagnosticSupportExport": {
    "files": [
      "diagnostics.json",
      "config/shape.json",
      "config/sanitized.json",
      "logs/openclaw-sanitized.jsonl",
      "summary.md"
    ],
    "sanitizedLogMessages": [
      "proof-short-read-one",
      "proof-short-read-two",
      "proof-short-read-three"
    ],
    "completeTail": true
  }
}
```

- Full successful proof command: `node --import tsx --input-type=module -` with a stdin script that imported the current branch modules by file URL, wrapped `fs.promises.open` before importing the log-tail consumers, called `readConfiguredLogTail({ limit: 10, maxBytes: 326 })`, called Gateway `logs.tail` with the same params, wrote a diagnostic support export, inspected `logs/openclaw-sanitized.jsonl` from the zip, and printed the JSON excerpt above.
- Focused regression: `node scripts/run-vitest.mjs src/logging/log-tail.test.ts` passed with 1 file and 2 tests, including repeated four-byte `fs.open().read()` returns against the real `readConfiguredLogTail` path.
- Targeted format: `node_modules\.bin\oxfmt.CMD --check --threads=1 src\logging\log-tail.ts src\logging\log-tail.test.ts` passed.
- Committed diff hygiene: `git diff --check upstream/main...HEAD` passed.
- Review proof: `python .agents\skills\autoreview\scripts\autoreview --mode local --engine codex --codex-bin C:\Users\86158\.codex\codex-pixel-autoreview.cmd` passed with no accepted/actionable findings.
- Duplicate search: open self PRs had no log-tail overlap; open and closed searches for `short reads log tail` and `log-tail short read` returned no overlapping PRs or issues. Open PR #74252 touches the same file for reset/truncation semantics but does not cover the short-read completeness invariant.

AI-assisted: yes. I reviewed the log-tail reader, active callers, sibling gateway diagnostic tail reader, focused tests, duplicate searches, runtime proof, and autoreview result before opening this PR.
